title: An fppf covering admits an etale-local finite locally free refinement
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $\{f_i:S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ be a small fppf covering [def-pc-fppf-site]. There exist a small jointly surjective family of etale morphisms $e_a:S\prime_a\to S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], surjective finite locally free morphisms $p_a:V_a\to S\prime_a$ [def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-pc-finite-locally-free], indices $i(a)\in I$, and morphisms $r_a:V_a\to S_{i(a)}$ such that $f_{i(a)}\circ r_a=e_a\circ p_a$ for every $a$. Empty schemes and empty indexing families are allowed.

proof.text: If $S=\varnothing$, take the empty etale family and empty finite locally free maps; all conditions are vacuous. If the original indexing family is empty, joint surjectivity in [def-pc-fppf-site] forces $S=\varnothing$. Hence assume below that $S$ is nonempty, and keep all index choices inside the fixed universes of [def-weil-size-convention].

source.place: Tag 0DET proof, initial reduction; Tag 05WN statement, empty cases

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fppf-local-qf-refinement] to obtain a small jointly surjective family $g_j:T_j\to S$ that is flat, locally of finite presentation, and locally quasi-finite, together with maps $T_j\to S_{i(j)}$ over $S$. For every $s\in S$, choose $j$ and $x\in T_j$ with $g_j(x)=s$; local quasi-finiteness means that $g_j$ is quasi-finite at $x$, so $x$ is isolated in the fibre by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-point-isolated].

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-finite-at-point-elementary] to $g_j:T_j\to S$, the point $s$ and the point $x$. It supplies an etale neighbourhood $(U,u)\to(S,s)$ and an open subscheme $V\subseteq T_j\times_SU$ such that $V\to U$ is finite and has a unique point over $u$ mapping to $x$. The base-change square gives the canonical equality of the composite $V\to T_j\to S$ with $V\to U\to S$, and the map $T_j\to S_{i(j)}$ restricts to the required refinement map from $V$ to $S_{i(j)}$.

The morphism $V\to U$ is also flat and locally of finite presentation: these properties hold for $T_j\to S$ by Step 2, pass to the base change $T_j\times_SU\to U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], and pass to the open subscheme $V$. Finiteness is retained under the subsequent base change by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence]. Thus $V\to U$ is finite locally free by [def-pc-finite-locally-free] (finite, flat, and locally of finite presentation). Since flat locally finitely presented maps are open [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], the image of $V\to U$ is an open neighbourhood of $u$. Replace $U$ by this image and $V$ by its inverse image; then $V\to U$ is surjective finite locally free, while the etale map to $S$ and the factorization through $S_{i(j)}$ remain unchanged after restriction.

source.place: Tag 0DET proof, third paragraph; Morphisms Tags 01U9, 01TS, 01WL, 01UA and 053N

proof.text: Repeat the construction for every $s\in S$ and retain one resulting $(U_s,u_s,V_s)$ for each choice. The family of etale maps $U_s\to S$ is jointly surjective because $s$ lies in the image of $U_s$; it is small by [def-weil-size-convention]. The maps $V_s\to S$ are surjective finite locally free after Step 4 and factor through the original member $S_{i(j)}\to S$, so they form the required refinement. Empty indexing families remain allowed, and no quasi-compactness, separatedness, or finiteness hypothesis on $S$ was introduced.
